## Current Astra source
Freshly read on this pass:
- https://github.com/harjassand/astra-research-knowledge/blob/main/cards/N1722-rare-ising-transition-capacity-and-unfinished-full-mean-construction.txt
- https://github.com/harjassand/astra-research-knowledge/blob/main/research/2026-11-04-ordered-ising-current-and-full-residence/source/P2_DIRECT_CURRENT_COMPLETE_RETURN.txt

The actual completed current return specifies the core, fixed zero-coupling contour diagonal, physical clock, and soft source convention used here. It states that exceptional boundary-current pruning needs a suitable normalized capacity lower bound. The checked source does not contain this particular nested-square thermal-prefix flow or the explicit bound here. This is not proof of absence in unacquired/held material or elsewhere.

Inherited source interfaces: acquired Z_A and core membership; the core-preserving filled-contour flip; M5/core normalizer ratio≤1/(1−u_r); actual decreasing soft committor and upward entrance current; fixed diagonal contour conventions. The package proves the new field interpolation and flow estimates rather than assuming a Gibbs entrance law.

## Strong primary comparator
Gaudillière, Milanesi, Vares, *Asymptotic exponential law for the transition time to equilibrium of the metastable kinetic Ising model with vanishing magnetic field*, arXiv1809.07044v2:
https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07044
https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.07044

Lemma4.5 already gives a normalized soft-capacity lower bound with the sharp thermal barrier, for sufficiently small field, using tailored finite Wulff-box sectors and conditioned random block flows. Normalized capacity lower bounds, thermal transport, and Thomson arguments are therefore pre-existing. Our finite coarse exponent is not an improvement on its sharp asymptotic exponent.

The specific practical distinction here is a finite explicit torus/core/majority-target bound, a polynomial edge-query representation, and a finite sparse-entry current certificate that removes the extensive allminus normalization loss. It leaves the actual dense-source physical growth/occupation problem open.
